prompt: Which part of the Bicep workflow needs an Azure subscription?
hint: What does Resource Manager do that the compiler does not?

choices.text: Compiling a `.bicep` file to JSON
choices.why: That runs on your computer, as this lesson shows.

choices.text: Running the linter over a file
choices.why: The linter is part of the same local program.

choices.text: Deploying the template
choices.why: Right. Deploying sends the JSON to Resource Manager, which needs a subscription.

choices.text: Decompiling an existing ARM template
choices.why: Decompiling reads a local JSON file and asks nobody.

prompt: In an ARM template, why does the container also list the storage account in `dependsOn`?
hint: How does Resource Manager create resources it is not told to order?

choices.text: ARM would otherwise create the two in parallel
choices.why: Right. ARM creates in parallel unless dependsOn orders it.

choices.text: Because the container's name does not mention the account
choices.why: It does mention it, in the format() call; ARM does not infer order from that.

choices.text: It grants the container access
choices.why: dependsOn orders creation; it grants nothing.

choices.text: It is optional, and only speeds the deployment up
choices.why: It slows nothing down and is required for correctness.

prompt: A template has `"name": "[paramaters('accountName')]"`, with the function name misspelt. When is that found?
hint: To a JSON parser, what is that value?

choices.text: When the file is saved, by any JSON editor
choices.why: It is a perfectly valid JSON string; a JSON editor has nothing to say.

choices.text: When Resource Manager evaluates the expression
choices.why: Right. The expression lives inside a string, which JSON does not look into.

choices.text: Never; Resource Manager ignores unknown functions
choices.why: It refuses the template when it evaluates the call.

choices.text: When git commits it
choices.why: git stores bytes; it has no opinion about templates.

prompt: `bicep decompile` prints a warning that decompilation is best effort. What should you do with the generated `.bicep`?
hint: Is it a translation or a draft?

choices.text: Deploy it at once; the warning appears every time
choices.why: The warning is there because the mapping is not guaranteed.

choices.text: Delete it and write the file by hand from the start
choices.why: A decompiled file is a useful starting point; discarding it wastes the work.

choices.text: Read it as a starting point, then build and lint it
choices.why: Right. It came out clean here, and you only know that by checking.

choices.text: Convert it back to JSON to compare the two by hand
choices.why: Building it does compile it back, but reading the Bicep is the point.

prompt: Match each ARM habit to what replaces it in Bicep.
hint: Each one is a mistake Bicep removes.

pairs.right: A symbolic reference implies the order

pairs.left: A child name built with slashes

right_distractors: A second service that deploys Bicep

prompt: Why does a deployment from Bicep need no permission beyond what an ARM deployment needs?

choices.text: Bicep deploys with its own built-in identity
choices.why: Bicep has no identity; it is a compiler on your machine.

choices.text: Bicep users get a role
choices.why: No role is granted for using a language.

choices.text: Bicep deployments skip Azure Policy
choices.why: Policy applies to every Resource Manager request, whatever wrote it.

choices.text: The compiled JSON, an ordinary ARM template
choices.why: Right. Resource Manager never sees Bicep at all.

prompt: In the JSON compiled from `shop.bicep`, how many resources carry a `dependsOn` that nobody wrote?
hint: Count the resources that name a parent.

prompt: `bicep build` compiled a file with `sku: { name: 'Standard_LRSS' }` and printed nothing. What does that tell you?
hint: How is the SKU's name typed in the schema Bicep has?

choices.text: That Standard_LRSS is a valid SKU name
choices.why: It is not; Resource Manager will refuse it at deployment.

choices.text: Its schema type is a plain string
choices.why: Right. A clean compile is evidence of shape, not of correct values.

choices.text: That warnings are off
choices.why: The other typo produced a warning in the same run.

choices.text: That the linter, not the compiler, checks SKUs
choices.why: Neither checks a value the schema types as a plain string.

prompt: A pipeline step runs `bicep build main.bicep` and passes. The log shows a BCP083 warning about a property that does not exist. Why did the step pass, and what fixes that?

choices.text: BCP083 is informational; there is nothing to fix
choices.why: It names a property that does not exist; the output would be wrong.

choices.text: The step ran the linter, which never fails
choices.why: It ran build, and lint rules can be raised to errors.

choices.text: A warning exits 0; make warnings fail the step
choices.why: Right. A pipeline that reads only the exit status ships warnings.

choices.text: The agent's Bicep is older than the developer's
choices.why: The warning appeared, so the version caught it; the issue is what happens next.

prompt: Why is an output carrying `listKeys()` dangerous even though the deployment succeeds?
hint: Where are a deployment's outputs kept?

choices.text: listKeys rotates the key each time it is called
choices.why: It reads the keys; it does not rotate them.

choices.text: The key ends up in the deployment history
choices.why: Right. That is what outputs-should-not-contain-secrets is about.

choices.text: Outputs are limited to 24 characters, so the key is cut
choices.why: There is no such limit; the whole key would be there.

choices.text: It makes the template fail on the second deployment
choices.why: It succeeds every time, which is what makes it easy to miss.

prompt: Lint rules are switched on, off or raised to errors in a file named ___ beside the Bicep files.
hint: A JSON file whose name starts with bicep.

prompt: `lint.bicep` wrote the location as the literal `'brazilsouth'`, and `bicep lint` said nothing about it. What is the right conclusion?
hint: Is there a rule for it?

choices.text: A literal location is good practice in Bicep
choices.why: A parameter or resourceGroup().location is the usual advice; the silence is about configuration.

choices.text: The linter cannot see string literals
choices.why: It saw the listKeys call inside a string in the same file.

choices.text: The rule is off unless bicepconfig.json turns it on
choices.why: Right. A linter is only the rules it was told to run.

choices.text: Resource Manager rewrites the location at deployment
choices.why: It deploys where the template says.

prompt: Put the life of the shop's storage template in order, from writing to the account existing.
hint: Two steps run on the laptop, two in Azure.
items: bicep build writes shop.json with the dependsOn filled in
Resource Manager receives the JSON and checks it against policy and permissions
The account is created, then its blob service, then the container
trap: Thinking Resource Manager reads the Bicep is the slip: it receives only the compiled JSON.
